subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox prune does not clean up workspace directory

question: Should maintainers replace/adopt the conflicting fork fix now for this focused prune-workspace cleanup, or fold the cleanup into the broader managed sandbox lifecycle work?
rationale: The bug remains clear, but the visible fork fix is conflicting and workspace deletion is state-destructive, while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98516 is a broader maintainer-owned lifecycle design that partially overlaps.

options.title: Land a narrow prune cleanup
options.body: Adopt or replace the fork candidate with a focused target-repo fix that deletes only eligible non-shared local sandbox workspaces and adds regression tests.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle design
options.body: Keep this issue open as focused evidence and make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98516 define the permanent cleanup contract first.

options.title: Close the fork candidate first
options.body: Resolve or supersede the conflicting fork PR before allowing any new repair path so there is one canonical implementation route.

recommendation.title: Land a narrow prune cleanup
recommendation.body: Adopt or replace the fork candidate with a focused target-repo fix that deletes only eligible non-shared local sandbox workspaces and adds regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest sandbox prune/workspace history and owns the broader related lifecycle issue.
